title: Identifying codes of the E8 root polytope
statement: Let G be the graph on the 240 roots of E8 in which two roots are adjacent when their inner product is 1 (the 1-skeleton of the Gosset polytope 4_21; 56 neighbours each). A set C of roots is an identifying code if the sets N[v] & C, where N[v] is v together with its neighbours, are nonempty and pairwise different for all 240 roots v. Determine the smallest size of an identifying code of G. Known: 9 <= minimum <= 15; find an identifying code with 14 or fewer roots, or prove a better lower bound.
submission: Text file: the vertex numbers (0 to 239) of the code in the checker's order: the roots doubled to integer vectors (two entries +-2 and six zeros, or eight entries +-1 with an even number of minus signs), sorted as tuples; see e8_graph in checkers/orig_codes.py.
score: the number of roots in the code (smaller is better)

best_known.source: Quantavane (Arhan Canli), 9 November 2026: an identifying code of 15 roots found by simulated annealing on the number of unidentified vertices (tools/graph_sets.py, 120 s)

context: Identifying codes (Karpovsky, Chakrabarty and Levitin, IEEE Trans. Inform. Theory 1998) locate a single faulty node from the set of codewords that see it; their counting bound gives |C| >= 2n/(Delta + 2) = 480/58 for this graph, so at least 9 roots. The E8 root system is the most symmetric configuration in eight dimensions (its graph is distance-regular with spectrum 56, 28, 8, -2, -4), and its large automorphism group (the Weyl group of order 696,729,600) suggests that orbit constructions could give much smaller codes than the 15 found by local search; the gap between 9 and 15 is wide. The 600-cell version of the question is the separate problem cell600-idcode.
references: M. G. Karpovsky, K. Chakrabarty, L. B. Levitin, On a new class of codes for identifying vertices in graphs, IEEE Trans. Inform. Theory 44 (1998) 599-611
J. H. Conway, N. J. A. Sloane, Sphere Packings, Lattices and Groups (Springer, 3rd ed. 1999), chapter 4 (the E8 root system)

novelty.verdict: new. Our arXiv searches found no identifying, locating or dominating code of the E8 root graph (the Gosset polytope 4_21), and a web search on identifying codes of polytope graphs found none either.
closest: Identifying codes of hypercubes, grids and other standard families; none for root-system or polytope graphs.

baseline.text: 15, held by Quantavane (Arhan Canli), 9 November 2026: the code in `refs/e8-idcode.txt` (simulated annealing, tools/graph_sets.py). Lower bound 9 from the counting bound 2n/(Delta + 2) = 480/58.
